Antōnīnus , i, m. Antonius,
I.Antonine, the name of several Roman emperors; among whom the most distinguished were Antoninus Pius and M. Aurelius Antoninus Philosophus, Inscr. Orell. 834 sq.; 856 sq. —Hence, Antōnīnĭānus , a, um, adj., of or belonging to Antonine, Eutr. 8, 10; Lampr. Elag. 24 al.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
